There are games that are difficult because they are designed to be mechanically punishing (like the Souls series, Ninja Gaiden, certain fighting games), but there is a difference between "Nintendo Hard" and a hard game.

For examples of modern games that are "Nintendo Hard", take a good look at similar genres as to what they made back in the day - platformers especially. They Bleed Pixels, Dustforce, Super Meat Boy, and many other precision platformers have come out that push the boundaries of difficulty once you get involved with them - but have evolved modern conveniences like infinite lives and save states, letting the "difficulty" come from the game itself rather than frustration of having to start over again and again.

If a game isn't at least a little bit challenging, whether mentally (strategy games with lots to think about), physically (FPS games based on reaction time and mouse/hand precision) or mechanically (whether with very challenging situations or with penalties like permadeath), then some people won't enjoy that game. There are people who just play games for the stories (Telltale games, the easiest Witcher 3 mode) but there are whole subgenres of games for those people too.

It can also be self reinforcing too. You play your game a lot, so you get good at it. You're then good enough that the game feels too easy/boring as a result, so you up the difficulty again. But then you have to test those changes, so you become good at the new version and find that too easy/boring... until you end up with a game that's too easy for you but too hard for everyone else.
